- If sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤ -0.50) or mixed, model often underestimates downside risk; add buffer below forecast or anticipate sharper declines.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at 1–2% below peak or introduce decay factor.
- When sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish (or vice versa), model lags in adjusting; delay forecast update or apply sentiment-weighted smoothing.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., after 80+ price peak, drops 10–20%), model often fails to recognize; apply decay or momentum correction to forecast.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overfit recent trends; use 18-day history as anchor, not 30-day trend, to avoid overreaction to short-term noise.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “0.00” or “-1.00” values, model underperforms; increase sensitivity to negative sentiment signals in forecasting.
